item.title: Trinity Sailing Hosts Women at the Helm 2026
item.description: On February 7th, Trinity Sailing hosted 18 teams (108 people) for their Women at the Helm Event at Royal St George Yacht Club in Dún Laoghaire. The 2026 event follows the inaugural Women at the Helm 2025 event, which also aimed to promote inclusivity and empower female athletes. The event, which was open to college students and alumni, was in a 3v3 racing format, where each team had three women at the wheel. item.title: Trinity Sailing Secures Historic Win in Oxford Top Gun Invitational
item.description: On the 24th of January, Trinity Sailing, represented by students Sam Ledoux, Georgia Goodbody, Trevor Bolger, Conor Lynch, Harry Twomey, and Orla Gilroy, competed in the Oxford Top Gun Invitational. Trinity Sailing achieved first place for the first time ever and became the second Irish team to win, earning an invitation to return next year to defend their title. item.title: Motaz Azaiza Receives Law Soc’s Praeses Elit Award
item.description: On February 5th, Dublin University Law Society (Law Soc) presented the Praeses Elit Award to Gazan photojournalist Motaz Azaiza in collaboration with Trinity Boycott, Divestment & Sanctions (BDS). On Instagram, Law Soc highlighted his “courageous and uncompromising photojournalism”, noting that “his images have documented not only devastation, but also resilience, dignity, and the enduring humanity of the people whose stories he tells”. item.title: Stoned To Death: Creativity, Collaborations and Pint Claddaghs
item.description: Bevin (Bev) Armstrong’s journey as a jeweller and creative started just over two years ago, as a form of art therapy. Since then, Armstrong has moved to London and Stoned To Death has evolved into a brand focused on creating gender-affirming jewellery with an Irish flair. In their studio, Bev does it all, from jewellery making to tattooing to print design.
